name: demand_jobs_per_unit_scale
description: CalculateJobsPerUnitOfDemand (corrected 2026-10-14): each output is f32(u32 percent) x 0.01f, one float32 multiply by the float constant 0.01f (0x3C23D70A), not a division by 100. The last bit differs from percent / 100: 33 gives 0.32999998 (0x3EA8F5C2), not 0.33000001 (0x3EA8F5C3); 30 gives 0x3E999999 (not 0x3E99999A), 99 0x3F7D70A3 (not 0x3F7D70A4), 40 0x3ECCCCCC (not 0x3ECCCCCD); 50, 1500 and 0 are exact either way. percent is unsigned: 0x80000000 gives +2^31 x 0.01f = 21474836 (0x4BA3D70A). GetJobsBySensus sums the three outputs in order, f32(f32(j1 + j2) + j3), and multiplies by the supply: with 33/30/99 % that is 1.6199999 (0x3FCF5C28) x 100 = 161.99998, truncated to 161 (the division would give 162); with 30/30/40 % it is 0.99999994 x 100 = 99.99999, 99 (not 100). The interface writes the outputs to jobs[1..3] of the caller's four floats; the core returns the three in that order. Expected bits from an independent Python model of the float32 steps.
